newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: SIMEX Brent crude firm despite Nigeria news.
newsitem.headline: SIMEX Brent crude firm despite Nigeria news.

text.p: SIMEX Brent stayed firmed despite news of Shell Nigeria resuming Bonny crude loading on support from a fall in distillate and gasoline stocks in the U.S, brokers said on Wednesday.
June was last traded at $18.14 per barrel, unchanged from its opening trade with a total of 95 lots seen traded at 0842 GMT.
Brokers said news of Shell Nigeria's resumption of Bonny crude oil loading did not affect the market.
The Nigerian unit of Royal Dutch Shell Group said its would resume the loading of the Bonny crude oil at noon after port workers called off a strike.
Shell had declared force majeure on some Bonny crude exports from Monday, when contractos began a stoppage.

Brokers said the fundementals were largely supported by API stocks data which showed a fall in distillates stock of 4.7 million barrels to 96.3 million last week. Gasoline stocks dropped 1.9 million to 195 million.
On ACCESS, June was last traded at $19.70, up 11 cents from its last official close.
